sam.name: Sam API — customer wallet top-ups
sam.summary: Lets a customer top up their own wallet: they transfer to your ShamCash or Syriatel Cash wallet through Sam, and the server asks Sam whether the transfer actually arrived. Once confirmed the balance is credited automatically, unless you turn on manual review below.
sam.apiKeyHelp: From your Sam dashboard. Stored on the server and never shown again.
sam.apiKeyKeepHelp: Leave blank to keep the current key.
sam.shamcashHelp: The wallet customers' money arrives in. Use “Show wallets” to find the right value.
sam.syriatelHelp: The phone number or cash code of your wallet.
sam.currencyHelp: What the customer pays in. Their wallet is credited in dollars either way.
sam.rateHelp: Used to convert the requested amount into pounds when the invoice is created.
sam.enabledHelp: When on, customers see it on the wallet top-up page.
sam.manualReviewLabel: Review every payment myself before crediting
sam.manualReviewHelp: Default: when Sam confirms the money arrived, the balance is credited immediately. With this on, even a confirmed payment waits for your approval on the top-up requests page.
sam.testHelp: Checks the key and lists the wallets linked to your Sam account with their balances.
sam.walletsEmpty: The key works, but no wallets are linked to this Sam account. Link one in your Sam dashboard and try again.
sam.walletsDescription: Loaded straight from Sam with the saved key. Seeing your wallet here means the key works.
sam.walletsNoKey: Add your Sam API key above and save. Your wallets, balances, and recent transfers will appear here.
sam.historyDescription: The last movements Sam reports on this wallet, whether or not they came from this store.
sam.historyEmpty: Sam reports no movements on this wallet yet.
sam.historyUnavailable: Sam could not read this wallet's transfers
sam.webhookDescription: Sam calls this address the moment a customer's payment lands, and the store credits the wallet. It contains a secret that proves the call really came from Sam — treat it like a password, and do not paste it anywhere public.
sam.webhookMissing: No secret yet — save your settings once to generate it.
sam.webhookRegenerateHelp: Only if you believe the current one leaked. Invoices already waiting for payment will stop crediting automatically.
sam.webhookRegenerated: A new secret is in place. Sam will use it for invoices from now on.
sam.webhookLocalBody: It points at this machine, so Sam's servers can never deliver a payment notification to it. Customer payments will not credit on their own until the store runs on its public address. Until then a customer can still confirm a payment from the payment page, and you can approve it from the top-up requests page.
sam.webhookInsecureBody: The callback carries a secret, so it must use HTTPS. Set your public site address to an https:// URL.

logging.name: Logging — Axiom
logging.summary: Where the store sends its own logs: every order, payment, provider call and failure, as searchable events. Without a destination the store still runs and still logs to the server console; nothing is stored where you can search it later.
logging.tokenHelp: Create an API token with ingest permission in your Axiom settings. Stored on the server and never shown again.
logging.tokenKeepHelp: Leave blank to keep the current token.
logging.datasetHelp: The Axiom dataset events are written to. Create it in Axiom first.
logging.domainHelp: The API host: api.axiom.co for a US workspace, api.eu.axiom.co for an EU one. A dataset's own edge address (…edge.axiom.co) also works.
logging.levelHelp: Lower levels mean more detail and more volume. Warnings and errors are what you want to be told about.
logging.enabledHelp: Turn off to stop sending without deleting the token. The console log is unaffected.
logging.testHelp: Writes one event to the dataset. If it appears in Axiom, the token and dataset are right.
logging.tested: Test event sent. It should appear in your Axiom dataset within a few seconds.

telegram.name: Telegram bot
telegram.summary: Your store bot on Telegram: customers browse the catalog, link their account, and get order alerts; you get the operations alerts.
telegram.botTokenHelp: Created in Telegram with @BotFather. Stored server-side and never shown again. The token only sends messages to the chat you register — it never lets anyone read customer data.
telegram.botTokenKeepHelp: Leave empty to keep the saved token.
telegram.featuresHelp: One bot serves both audiences. The customer side works from any chat; your alerts go to the owner chat you link with /start.
features: Customers browse the catalog, deals, and search from the chat — no images, no checkout needed to look.
Customers link their account with a code and see their orders, wallet, and order updates in their language.
Customers open support threads and get a one-tap sign-in link straight from the chat.
You get new order, failure, recharge, support, and low-wallet alerts in the owner chat.
The menu (☰) shows every command once installed.
telegram.commandsHelp: Makes the ☰ button appear in Telegram with all commands. Safe to run again any time.
telegram.enabledHelp: When on, queued alerts are sent to your chat on the Worker's five-minute schedule. Turning it off keeps the token.
telegram.alertTypesHelp: Which events reach your Telegram. The store never waits on Telegram, so turning these on cannot slow checkout or delivery.
telegram.testHelp: Checks the token with Telegram and shows the bot's username and webhook state.
telegram.chatNotLinked: The owner chat is not linked yet. Open the bot in Telegram and send /start from the chat that should receive alerts.
telegram.webhookHelp: Registers the bot's webhook with Telegram. It points at a Supabase Edge Function (like the G2Bulk callback), so it works however the store is deployed. The dashboard performs the setWebhook call itself; you do not need to run curl.
telegram.webhookRegenerateHelp: Generates a new secret and tells Telegram to use it. Only needed if you believe the current one leaked.
telegram.webhookSecretHelp: Telegram verifies every update against this value. Treat it like a password: if you set a TELEGRAM_WEBHOOK_SECRET Worker secret, it should match this. Regenerate if you think it leaked.
